evidence.s1: The label and ornaments stay distinctly light or dark across all eight works; the record separates source, declared tone and per-line rendered readings.
evidence.s2: One left-hand label window holds the reading task in both schemes, with navigation and audio as ornaments rather than extra windows.
evidence.s3: The record gives the label a 461 px shorter span and thickness 8 shared with its two ornaments, whose labels remain readable in both schemes.
evidence.s4: The painting fills the viewport and remains exposed on every side of the stationary label through both schemes and scroll positions.
evidence.s5: The record declares regular only, and label, room navigation and guide show a consistent material family in both schemes.
evidence.s6: No clear glass is used; the regular label and ornaments sit over the paintings in both schemes.
evidence.s7: No navigation or guide control is tinted in either scheme; all colour belongs to the paintings.
evidence.s8: The light label carries blurred painting colour and the dark label a smoked body; the record specifies runtime material rather than substitute fills or blur.
evidence.s9: The label has fixed 32 px corners and the bottom ornaments are 52 px capsules with 26 px radii, recorded and visually consistent in both schemes.
evidence.s10: The bottom-scrolled data inset has the recorded 18 px radius from 32 minus 14, while the whole-work frame uses 4 from 32 minus 28.
evidence.s11: The guide play control and navigation controls are circular or capsule forms inside the bottom capsule housings in both schemes.
evidence.s12: Room navigation and audio transport occupy two separate bottom glass groups, each collecting one related task in both schemes.
evidence.s13: The bottom-left room-index text button shares its glass capsule with the previous and next icon buttons in both schemes.
evidence.s14: The two ornament housings carry the material behind plain control contents, with no separate glass applied to play glyphs or index text.
evidence.s15: Navigation items share one capsule and audio items another; their recorded 24 px separation keeps the bottom pair intentionally distinct.
evidence.s16: Middle and bottom captures move the label contents through faded inner edges while the rounded host and both bottom ornaments remain fixed in both schemes.
evidence.s17: Paintings supply texture beneath the label and ornaments, including visible variation in Monet’s softer fog phase rather than a uniform backdrop.
evidence.s18: Label prose and ornament labels remain readable in both schemes; the record reports no under-floor lines, with the worst GPU reading 4.93:1.
evidence.s19: unread: reduced transparency preserves the light label and the record verifies live reduced motion, but no increased-contrast result is recorded or captured.
evidence.s20: The label and ornaments have no authored host fill or border in the record; their grading is painted into the environmental canvas, not a host scrim.
evidence.s21: unread: the record keeps the glass stationary and names runtime press motion, but neither captures nor a recorded press observation establish pointer glow and flex.
evidence.s22: Room-navigation and audio-guide contents are monochrome in light and dark, leaving saturated colour to the paintings.
evidence.s23: Dark controls on pale ornaments and pale controls on dark ornaments separate from the painting colours in all eight phase pairs.
evidence.s24: The label uses recorded primary child ink at weights 500–700, with per-line measurements and the worst line gating; no module prose is present.
evidence.s25: The bottom-scrolled data table has a darker child fill inside the label in both schemes, not another glass host or a light-on-light stack.
evidence.s26: Both bottom ornaments align within the label width and sit outside it by the recorded runtime-derived 64 px gap on separate overlay groups.
evidence.s27: The whole-work thumbnail is an opaque image in the recorded concentric 4 px frame within the left label in both schemes.
evidence.s28: No chromatic accent is applied to lightweight type or thin marks on the label or ornaments in either scheme.
evidence.s29: The label and ornament family is untinted; each phase’s identity comes from its full-screen painting and whole-work image.
evidence.s30: The record reports CSS two-layer at DPR 1 and collapsed at DPR 2 with present-host areas; CSS and forced-colour captures preserve the label and artwork outline, and extrapolation is explicit.
